verses.text: And Josias helde the Feast of the Passeouer in Jerusalem to his Lord, and offered the Passeouer the fourteenth day of the first moneth:
Hauing set the Priests according to their daily courses, being arayed in long garments, in the Temple of the Lord.

And he spake to the Leuites the holy ministers of Yahsharala, that they should hallow themselues to the Lord, to set the holy Arke of the Lord, in the house that king Solomon the son of Dauid had built:
And said, You shall no more beare the Arke on your shoulders: now therefore serve the Lord your Alahayam, and minister to his people Yahsharala, and prepare you after your families and kinreds.

According as Dauid the king of Yahsharala prescribed, & according to the magnificence of Solomon his son: & standing in the Temple according to the seuerall dignitie of the families of you the Leuites, who minister in the presence of your brothers the children of Yahsharala.
Offer the Passeouer in order, and make ready the sacrifices for your brothers, and keepe the Passeouer according to the commaundement of the Lord, which was given to Moyses.

And to the people that was found there, Josias gave thirtie thousand lambes, and kids, and three thousand calues: these things were given of the kings allowance, according as he promised to the people, to the Priestes, and to the Leuites.
And Helkias, Zacharias, and Sielus the gouernours of the Temple, gave to the Priests for the Passeouer, two thousand and six hundred sheepe, and three hundreth calues.

And Iechonias, and Samaias, and Nathanael his brother, and Assabias, and Ochiel, and Ioram captaines over thousands, gave to the Leuites for the Passeouer five thousand sheepe, and seven hundreth calues.
And when these things were done, the Priests and Leuites hauing the vnleauened bread, stood in very comely order according to the kinreds,
And according to the seuerall dignities of the fathers, before the people, to offer to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moyses: And thus did they in the morning.
And they rosted the Passeouer with fire, as appertaineth: as for the sacrifices, they sodde them in brasse pots, and pannes with a good sauour.
And set them before all the people, and afterward they prepared for themselues, and for the Priests their brothers the sons of Aaron.
For the Priests offered the fat until night: and the Leuites prepared for themselues, and the Priests their brothers the sons of Aaron.
The holy Singers also, the sons of Asaph, were in their order, according to the appointment of Dauid, to wit, Asaph, Zacharias, and Ieduthun, who was of the kings retinue.
Moreouer the porters were at every gate: it was not lawfull for any to goe from his ordinary seruice: for their brothers the Leuites prepared for them.
Thus were the things that belonged to the sacrifices of the Lord accomplished in that day, that they might hold the Passeouer,
And offer sacrifices on the altar of the Lord, according to the commandement of king Josias.
So the children of Yahsharala which were present, held the Passeouer at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days.
And such a Passeouer was not kept in Yahsharala since the time of the Prophet Samuel.
Yea all the kings of Yahsharala held not such a Passeouer as Josias, and the Priests and the Leuites, & the Jews held with all Yahsharala that were found dwelling at Jerusalem.
In the eighteenth yeere of the reigne of Josias was this Passeouer kept.
And the workes of Josias were vpright before his Lord with an heart full of godlinesse.

As for the things that came to passe in his time, they were written in former times, concerning those that sinned, and did wickedly against the Lord above all people and kingdomes, and how they grieued him exceedingly, so that the words of the Lord rose up against Yahsharala.
Now after all these acts of Josias, it came to passe that Pharao the king of Egypt came to raise warre at Carchamis on Euphrates: and Josias went out against him.
But the king of Egypt sent to him saying, What have I to do with you, O king of Iudea?

I am not sent out from the Lord Alahayam against you: for my warre is on Euphrates, and now the Lord is with mee, yea the Lord is with mee hasting me forward: Depart from me and be not against the Lord.
Howbeit Josias did not turne backe his chariot from him, but vndertooke to fight with him, not regarding the words of the Prophet Ieremie, spoken by the mouth of the Lord:
But ioyned battell with him in the plaine of Magiddo, and the princes came against king Josias.
Then said the king to his servants, carry me away out of the battell for I am very weake: and immediately his servants tooke him away out of the battell.
Then gate he up on his second chariot, and being brought backe to Jerusalem, dyed, and was buried in his fathers sepulchre.

And in all Iury they mourned for Josias, yea Ieremie the Prophet lamented for Josias, and the cheefe men with the women made lamentation for him to this day: and this was given out for an ordinance to be done continually in all the nation of Yahsharala.

These things are written in the book of the stories of the kings of Iudah, and every one of the acts that Josias did, and his glory, and his understanding in the law of the Lord, and the things that he had done before, and the things now recited, are reported in the books of the Kings of Yahsharala and Iudea.
And the people tooke Ioachaz the son of Josias, and made him king in stead of Josias his father, when he was twenty and three yeeres old.
And he reigned in Iudea and in Jerusalem three moneths: and then the King of Egypt deposed him from reigning in Jerusalem.
And he set a taxe on the land of an hundreth talents of siluer, and one talent of gold.
The king of Egypt also made king Ioacim his brother king of Iudea and Jerusalem.
And he bound Ioacim and the nobles: but Zaraces his brother he apprehended, and brought him out of Egypt.
Five and twenty yeere old was Ioacim when he was made king in the land of Iudea and Jerusalem, and he did evil before the Lord.
Therefore against him Nabuchodonosor the King of Babylon came up, and bound him with a chaine of brasse, and carried him to Babylon.
Nabuchodonosor also tooke of the holy vessels of the Lord, and carried them away, and set them in his own temple at Babylon.
But those things that are recorded of him, and of his vncleannes, and impietie, are written in the Chronicles of the kings.
And Ioacim his son reigned in his stead: he was made king being eighteene yeeres old,
And reigned but three moneths and ten days in Jerusalem, and did evil before the Lord.
So after a yere Nabuchodonosor sent, and caused him to be brought into Babylon with þ holy vessels of þ Lord,
And made Zedechias king of Iudea and Jerusalem, when he was one and twenty yeeres old, and he reigned eleuen yeeres:
And he did evil also in the sight of the Lord, & cared not for the words that were spoken to him, by the Prophet Ieremie from the mouth of the Lord.

And after that king Nabuchodonosor had made him to sweare by the Name of the Lord, he forswore himself, and rebelled, and hardening his necke, and his heart, he transgressed the lawes of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala.

The gouernours also of the people and of the priests did many things against the lawes, and passed al the pollutions of all nations, and defiled the Temple of the Lord which was sanctified in Jerusalem.
Neuerthelesse, the Alahayam of their fathers sent by his messenger to call them backe, because he spared them and his tabernacle also:
But they had his messengers in derision, and looke when the Lorde spake to them, they made a sport of his prophets,
So farre foorth that he being wroth with his people for their great vngodlinesse, commanded the kings of the Caldees to come up against them.
Who flew their yong men with the sword, yea even within the compasse of their holy Temple, & spared neither yong man nor maid, old man nor child among them, for he deliuered all into their hands.
And they tooke all the holy vessels of the Lord, both great and small, with the vessels of the Ark of Alahayam, and the kings treasures, and caried them away into Babylon.
As for the house of the Lord they burnt it, brake down the walles of Jerusalem, set fire on her towres.
And as for her glorious things, they never ceased til they had consumed and brought them all to nought, and the people that were not slaine with the sword, he caried to Babylon:
Who became servants to him and his children, till the Persians reigned, to fulfill the word of the Lord spoken by the mouth of Ieremie:
Untill the land had enioyed her Sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she rest, until the full terme of seuentie yeeres.
In the first yeere of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the worde of the Lorde might be accomplished, that he had promised by the mouth of Ieremie:
The Lord raised up the spirit of Cyrus the king of the Persians, and he made proclamation thorow al his kingdome, and also by writing,
Saying, Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians, The Lord of Yahsharala the most high Lord, has made me king of the whole world,
And commanded me to build him an house at Jerusalem in Iurie.

If therefore there be any of you that are of his people, let the Lord, even his Lord be with him, and let him goe up to Jerusalem that is in Iudea, and build the house of the Lord of Yahsharala: for he is the Lord that dwells in Jerusalem.
Whoever then dwell in the places about, let them helpe him, those I say that are his neighbours, with gold and with siluer,
With gifts, with horses, and with cattell, and other things, which have been set forth by vowe, for the Temple of the Lord at Jerusalem.

¶ Then the chiefe of the families of Iudea, and of the tribes of Beniamin stood up: the priests also and the Leuites, and all they whose mind the Lord had moued to goe up, and to build an house for the Lord at Jerusalem,
And they that dwelt round about them, and helped them in all things with siluer and gold, with horses and cattell, and with very free gifts of a great number whose mindes were stirred up thereto.
King Cyrus also brought foorth the holy vessels which Nabuchodonosor had caried away from Jerusalem, and had set up in his temple of idoles.
Now when Cyrus king of the Persians had brought them foorth, he deliuered them to Mithridates his treasurer:
And by him they were deliuered to Sanabassar þ gouernour of Iudea.

And this was the number of them, a thousand golden cuppes, and a thousand of siluer, censers of siluer twenty nine, vials of gold thirtie, and of siluer two thousand four hundred and ten, and a thousand other vessels.
So all the vessels of gold, and of siluer which were caried away, were five thousand, four hundred, threescore and nine.
These were brought back by Sanabassar, together with them of the captiuity, from Babylon to Jerusalem.

But in the time of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Belemus, and Mithridates, and Tabellius, and Rathumus, and Beeltethmus, and Semellius the Secretarie, with others that were in commission with them, dwelling in Samaria and other places, wrote to him against them that dwelt in Iudea and Jerusalem, these letters following.
To King Artaxerxes our lord, Your servants Rathumus the story writer, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest of their counsell, and the Iudges that are in Coelosyria and Phenice.

Be it now knowen to the lord the king, that the Jews that are come up from you to us, being come into Jerusalem (that rebellious and wicked city,) do build the market places, and repaire the walles of it, and do lay the foundation of the Temple.
Now if this city, and the walles of it be made up again, they will not only refuse to give tribute, but also rebell against kings.
And forasmuch as the things pertaining to the Temple, are now in hand, we thinke it meete not to neglect such a matter,
But to speak to our lord the king, to the intent that if it be your pleasure, it may be sought out in the books of your fathers:
And you will finde in the Chronicles, what is written concerning these things, and will understand that that city was rebellious, troubling both kings and cities:
And that the Jews were rebellious, and raised alwayes warres therin, for the which cause even this city was made desolate.
Therefore now we do declare to you, (O lord the king) that if this city be built again, and the walles of it set up anew, you will from hencefoorth have no passage into Corlosyria and Phenice.

Then the King wrote backe again to Rathumus the storie-writer, to Beeltethmus, to Semellius the scribe, and to the rest that were in commission, and dwellers in Samaria and Syria, and Phenice, after this maner.
I have read the Epistle which you have sent to mee: therefore I commanded to make diligent search, and it has been found, that that city was from the beginning practising against Kings.
And the men in it were given to rebellion, and warre, and that mightie Kings and fierce were in Jerusalem, who reigned and exacted tributes in Coelosyria and Phenice.
Now therefore I have commanded to hinder those men from building the city, and heed to be taken that there be no more done in it,
And that those wicked workers proceed no further to the annoyance of Kings.

Then king Artaxerxes his letters being read, Rathumus and Semellius the scribe, and the rest that were in commission with them, remoouing in have towards Jerusalem with a troupe of horsemen, and a multitude of people in battell aray, began to hinder the builders, and the building of the Temple in Jerusalem ceased until the second yeere of the reigne of Darius King of the Persians.
Now when Darius reigned, he made a great feast to all his Subiects and to all his houshold, and to all the princes of Media and Persia,
And to all the gouernours and captaines, and lieutenants that were under him, from Iudia to Ethiopia, of an hundreth twenty and seven prouinces.
And when they had eaten and drunken, and being satisfied were gone home, then Darius the king went into his bed chamber, and slept, and soone after awaked.
Then three yong men that were of the guard, that kept the kings body, spake one to another:
Let every one of us speak a sentence: he that shall overcome, & whose sentence shall seeme wiser then the others, to him shall the king Darius give great gifts, and great things in token of victory:
As to be clothed in purple, to drink in golde, and to sleepe on golde, and a chariot with bridles of golde, and an head-tyre of fine linen, and a chaine about his necke:
And he shall sit next to Darius, because of his wisedome, and shall be called, Darius his cousin.
And then every one wrote his sentence, sealed it, and laide it under king Darius his pillow,

And sayd, that when the king is risen, some will give him the writings, and of whose side the king, and the three princes of Persia shall judge, that his sentence is the wisest, to him shall the victory be given as was appointed.
The first wrote: Wine is the strongest.
The second wrote: The King is strongest.
The third wrote; Women are strongest, but above all things truth beareth away the victory.
¶ Now when the king was risen up, they tooke their writings, and deliuered them to him, and so he read them.
And sending foorth, he called all the Princes of Persia and Media, and the gouernours, and the captaines, and the lieutenants, and the chiefe officers,
And sate him down in the royall seate of Judgment, and the writings were read before them:
And he said, Call the young men, and they shall declare their own sentences: so they were called, and came in.
And he said to them, Declare to us your mind, concerning the writings. Then began the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine;
And he said thus: O you men, how exceeding strong is wine! it causeth all men to erre that drinke it:
It makes the mind of the king, and of the fatherlesse childe to be all one of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poore man and of the rich:
It turneth also every thought into iollitie and mirth, so that a man remembreth neither sorow nor debt:
And it makes every heart rich, so that a man remembreth neither king nor gouernour, and it makes to speak all things by talents:
And when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and brothers, and a litle after draw out swords:
But when they are from the wine, they remember not what they have done.
O you men, is not wine the strongest, that enforceth to do thus? And when he had so spoken, he helde his peace.
Then the second that had spoken of the strength of the King, began to say;
O you men, do not men excel in strength, that beare rule over Sea and land, and all things in them?
But yet the King is more mighty: for he is lord of all these things, and has dominion over them, and whatsoeuer he commandeth them, they do:
If you bid them make warre the one against the other, they do it: if he send them out against the enemies, they goe, and breake down mountaines, walles and towres.
They slay and are slaine, and transgresse not the Kings commandement: if they get the victory, they bring all to the King, as well the spoile as all things else.

Likewise for those that are no souldiers, and have not to do with warres, but use husbandrie; when they have reaped again, that which they had sowen, they bring it to the King, and compell one another to pay tribute to the King.
And yet he is but one man; if he commaund to kill, they kill, if he command to spare, they spare.
If he command to smite, they smite; if he command to make desolate, they make desolate; if he command to build, they build:
If he command to cut down, they cut down; if he command to plant, they plant.
So all his people and his armies obey him; furthermore he lieth down, he eateth and drinketh, & takes his rest.
And these keepe (watch) round about him, neither may any one depart, and do his own businesse, neither disobey they him in any thing.
O you men, how should not the King be mightiest, when in such sort he is obeyed? and he held his tongue.
¶ Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth (this was Zorobabel) beganne to speak.
O you men, it is not the great King, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or has the lordship over them, are they not women?
Women have borne the King and all the people, that beare rule by sea and land.
Even of thē came they: & they nourished them up that planted the vineyards from whence the wine commeth.
These also make garments for men; these bring glory to men, and without women cannot men be.
Yea and if men have gathered together gold and siluer, or any other goodly thing, do they not love a woman, which is comely in favor and beautie?

And letting all those things goe, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fixe their eyes fast on her; and have not all men more desire to her, then to siluer or gold, or any goodly thing whatsoeuer?
A man leaueth his own father that brought him up, and his own countrie, and cleaueth to his wife.
He stickes not to spend his life with his wife, and remembreth neither father, nor mother, nor country.
By this also you must know, that women have dominion over you: do you not labour and toyle, and give and bring all to the woman?
Yea a man takes his sword, and goes his way to rob, and to steale, to saile on the sea, and on riuers,
And looketh on a lyon, and goes in the darknesse, and when he has stolen, spoiled and robbed, he bringeth it to his love.
Therefore a man loueth his wife better then father and mother.
Yea many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes:
Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned for women.
And now do you not belieue me? is not the King great in his power? do not all regions fear to touch him?
Yet did I see him and Apame the Kings concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the King,
And taking the crowne from the Kings head, and setting it on her own head; she also strooke the King with her left hand.

And yet for all this, the King gaped and gazed on her with open mouth: if she laughed on him, he laughed also: but if she tooke any displeasure at him, the King was faine to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again.
O you men, how can it be but women should be strong, seeing they do thus?
Then the king & the princes looked one on another: so he began to speak of the truth.

O you men, are not women strong? great is the earth, high is the heaven, swift is the Sunne in his course, for he compasseth the heavens round about, and fetcheth his course again to his own place in one day.
Is he not great that makes these things? therefore great is the truth, and stronger then all things.
All the earth calleth on the truth, & the heaven blesseth it, all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no vnrighteous thing.

Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked, and such are all their wicked workes, and there is no truth in them. In their vnrighteousnes also they shall perish.
As for the truth it endureth, and is alwayes strong, it liueth and conquereth for euermore.
With her there is no accepting of persons, or rewards, but she does the things that are just, and refraineth from all vniust and wicked things, and all men do well like of her workes.
Neither in her judgment is any vnrighteousnesse, & she is the strength, kingdome, power and maiestie of all ages. Blessed be the Alahayam of truth.
And with that he held his peace, and al the people then shouted and said, Great is truth, and mightie above all things.
Then saide the king to him, Aske what you will, more then is appointed in the writing, and we wil give it you, because you are found wisest, and you will sit next me, and will be called my cousin.
Then said he to the king, Remember your vow which you have vowed to build Jerusalem in the day when you camest to the kingdome,
And to send away all the vessels that were taken away out of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart, when he vowed to destroy Babylon, and to send them again thither.
You also have vowed to build up the Temple, which the Edomites burnt when Iudea was made desolate by the Chaldees.

And now, O lord the king, this is that which I require, and which I desire of you, and this is the princely liberalitie proceeding from your self: I desire therefore that you make good the vow, the performance wherof with your own mouth you have vowed to the king of heaven.

Then Darius the king stood up and kissed him, and wrote letters for him to all the treasurers and lieutenants, and captaines and gouernours that they should safely conuey on their way, both him, and all those that go up with him to build Jerusalem.

He wrote letters also to the lieutenants that were in Coelosyria and Phenice, and to them in Libanus, that they should bring Cedar wood from Libanus to Jerusalem, and that they should build the city with him

Moreouer he wrote for all the Jews that went out of his realme up into Iurie, concerning their freedome, that no officer, no ruler, no lieutenant, nor treasurer, should forcibly enter into their dores,
And that all the country which they hold, should be free without tribute, & that the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held,
Yea that there should be yereely given twenty talents to þ building of the Temple, until you time that it were built,
And other tenne talents yeerely, to maintaine the burnt offerings on the Altar every day (as they had a commandement to offer seuenteene)
And that all they that went from Babylon to build the city, should have free liberty as well they as their posteritie, and all the priests that went away.
He wrote also concerning the charges, and the priests vestments in which they minister:
And likewise for the charges of the Leuites, to be given them, until the day that the house were finished, and Jerusalem builded up.
And he commanded to give to all that kept the city, pensions and wages.
He sent away also all the vessels frō Babylon that Cyrus had set apart, and all that Cyrus had given in commandement, the same charged he also to be done, and sent to Jerusalem.
Now when this yong man was gone forth, he lifted up his face to heaven toward Jerusalem, and praised the king of heaven,
And said, From you commeth victory, from you commeth wisedom, and your is the glory, & I am your servant.
Blessed are you who have given me wisedom: for to you I give thanks, O Lord of our fathers.
And so he tooke the letters, and went out, and came to Babylon, and told it all his brothers.
And they praised the Alahayam of their fathers: because he had given them freedome and libertie
To goe up, and to build Jerusalem, and the Temple which is called by his Name, and they feasted with instruments of musick, & gladnes seven days.
After this were the principall men of the families chosen according to their tribes, to go up with their wiues, and sons, and daughters, with their men-servants and maid-servants, and their cattel.
And Darius sent with them a thousand horsmen, til they had brought them backe to Jerusalem safely, and with musicall tabrets and flutes:
And all their brothers played, and he made them goe up together with them.
And these are the names of the men which went up, according to their families, among their tribes, after their seuerall heads.

The Priestes the sons of Phinees, the son of Aaron: Jesus the son of Iosedec, the son of Saraias, and Ioachim the son of Zorobabel, the son of Salathiel of the house of Dauid, out of the kindred of Phares, of the tribe of Iuda;
Who spake wise sentences before Darius the king of Persia, in the second yeere of his reigne, in the moneth Nisan, which is the first moneth.
And these are they of Iewrie that came up from the captiuitie, where they dwelt as strangers, whom Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon:

And they returned to Jerusalem, and to the other parts of Iurie every man to his own city, who came with Zorobabel, with Jesus, Nehemias, and Zacharias, and Reesaias, Enenius, Mardocheus, Beelsarus, Aspharasus, Reelius, Roimus, and Baana their guides.
The number of them of the nation, and their gouernours: sons of Phoros two thousand an hundred seuentie and two: the sons of Saphat four hundred seuentie and two;
The sons of Ares seven hundred fifty and six:
The sons of Phaath Moab, two thousand eight hundred & twelue:
The sons of Elam, a thousand two hundred fifty and four: the sons of Zathui, nine hundred fourtie and five: the sons of Corbe seven hundred and five: the sons of Bani, six hundred fourtie and eight:
The sons of Bebai, six hundred twenty and three: the sons of Sadas, three thousand two hundred twenty and two:
The sons of Adonican, six hundred sixtie and seven: the sons of Bagoi, two thousand sixtie and six: the sons of Adin, four hundred fifty and four:
The sons of Aterezias, ninetie and two: the sons of Ceilan and Azetas, threescore and seven: the sons of Azuran, four hundred thirtie & two.
The sons of Ananias, an hundred and one: the sons of Arom thirtie two, and the sons of Bassa, three hundred twenty and three: the sons of Azephurith, an hundred and two:
The sons of Meterus, three thousand and five: the sons of Bethlomon, an hundred twenty and three.
They of Netophah fifty and five: they of Anathoth, an hundred fifty and eight: they of Bethsamos, fourtie and two:
They of Kiriathiarius, twenty and five: they of Caphira and Beroth, seven hundred fourtie and three: they of Pyra, seven hundred:
They of Chadias and Ammidioi, four hundred twenty and two: they of Cyrama, and Gabdes, six hundred twenty and one:
They of Macalon, an hundred twenty and two: they of Betolius fifty and two: the sons of Nephis, an hundred fifty and six.
The sons of Calamolalus, and Onus, seven hundred twenty and five: the sons of Ierechus, two hundred fourtie and five:
The sons of Annaas, three thousand three hundred and thirtie:
The Priests, the sons of Ieddu, the son of Jesus, among the sons of Sanasib, nine hundred seuentie and two: the sons of Meruth, a thousand fifty and two:
The sons of Phassaron, a thousand fourtie and seven: the sons of Carme a thousand and seuenteene.
The Leuites: the sons of Iessue, and Cadmiel, and Banuas, and Sudias, seuentie and four.
The holy singers: the sons of Asaph an hundred twenty and eight.
The porters: the sons of Salum, the sons of Iatal, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Dacobi, the sons of Teta, the sons of Sami, in all an hundred thirty and nine.
The servants of the Temple: the sons of Esau, the sons of Asipha, the sons of Tabaoth, the sons of Ceras: the sons of Sud, the sons of Phaleas, the sons of Labana, the sons of Graba:
The sons of Acua, the sons of Uta, the sons of Cetab, the sons of Agaba, the sons of Subai, the sons of Anan, the sons of Cathua, the sons of Geddur:

The sons of Airus, the sons of Daisan, the sons of Noeba, the sons of Chaseba, the sons of Gazera, the sons of Azia, the sons of Phinees, the sons of Azara, the sons of Bastai, the sons of Asana the sons of Meani, the sons of Naphisi, the sons of Acub, the sons of Asipha, the sons of Assur, the sons of Pharacim, the sons of Basaloth.
The sons of Meeda: the sons of Coutha, the sons of Charea, the sons of Chareus, the sons of Aserer, the sons of Thomoi, the sons of Nasith, the sons of Atipha.
The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Azaphion, the sons of Pharira, the sons of Ioeli, the sons of Lozon, the sons of Isdael, the sons of Sapheth:

The sons of Hagia, the sons of Phacareth, the sons of Sabie, the sons of Sarothie, the sons of Masias, the sons of Gar, the sons of Addus, the sons of Suba, the sons of Apherra, the sons of Barodis, the sons of Sabat, the sons of Allom.
All the ministers of the Temple, and the sons of the servants of Solomon, were three hundred seuenty & two.
These came up from Thermeleth, and Thelersas, Charaathalar leading them and Aalar.
Neither could they shewe their families, nor their stock, how they were of Yahsharala: the sons of Ladan, the sons of Ban, the sons of Necodan, six hundred fifty and two.

And of the Priests that vsurped the office of the Priesthood, and were not found, the sons of Obdia: the sons of Accoz, the sons of Addus, who married Augia one of the daughters of Berzelus, and was named after his name.
And when the description of the kinred of these men was sought in the Register, and was not found, they were remooued from executing the office of the Priesthood.
For to them said Nehemias, and Atharias, that they should not be partakers of the holy things, till there arose up an high Priest, clothed with Doctrine and Truth.
So of Yahsharala from them of twelue yeeres old and vpward, they were all in number fourtie thousand, besides men servants and women servants, two thousand three hundred and sixtie.
Their men servants and handmaids were seven thousand three hundred fourtie and seven: the singing men and singing women, two hundred fortie and five.
Four hundred thirtie and five camels, seven thousand thirtie and six horses, two hundred fourtie and five mules, five thousand five hundred twenty & five beasts used to the yoke.
And certain of the chiefe of their families, when they came to the Temple of Alahayam that is in Jerusalem, vowed to set up the house again in his own place according to their abilitie:
And to give into the holy treasurie of the workes, a thousand pounds of golde, five thousand of siluer, and an hundred priestly vestments.
And so dwelt the Priests, and the Leuites, and the people in Jerusalem, and in the country: the Singers also, and the Porters, and all Yahsharala in their villages.

But when the seventh moneth was at hand, and when the children of Yahsharala were every man in his own place, they came all together with one consent into the open place of the first gate, which is towards the East.
Then stood up Jesus the son of Iosedec, and his brothers the Priests, and Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and his brothers, and made ready the Altar of the Alahayam of Yahsharala,
To offer burnt sacrifices on it, according as it is expresly commanded in the book of Moses the man of Alahayam.

And there were gathered to them out of the other nations of the land, and they erected the Altar on his own place, because all the nations of the land were at enmitie with them, and oppressed them, and they offered sacrifices according to the time, and burnt offerings to the Lord both morning, and euening.
Also they held the feast of Tabernacles, as it is commanded in the law, and offered sacrifices daily as was meet:
And after, that the continuall oblations, and the sacrifice of the Sabbaths, and of the new Moones, and of all holy feasts.
And all they that had made any vow to Alahayam, beganne to offer sacrifices to Alahayam from the first day of the seventh moneth, although the Temple of the Lord was not yet built.
And they gave to the Masons and Carpenters, money, meate and drinke with cheerefulnesse.

Unto them of Sidon also and Tyre, they gave carres that they should bring Cedar trees from Libanus, which should be brought by flotes to the haven of Ioppe, according as it was commanded them by Cyrus King of the Persians.

And in the second yeere and second moneth, after his comming to the Temple of Alahayam at Jerusalem, beganne Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Iosedec, and their brothers and the priests, and the Leuites, and all they that were come to Jerusalem out of the captiuity:
And they layd the foundation of the house of Alahayam, in the first day of the second moneth, in the second yeere after they were come to Iury & Jerusalem.

And they appointed the Lenites from twenty yeeres old, over the workes of the Lord. Then stood up Jesus and his sons, and brothers, and Cadmiel his brother, & the sons of Madiabun, with the sons of Ioda the son of Eliadun, with their sons and brothers, all Leuites, with one accord seters forward of the businesse, labouring to aduance the workes in the house of Alahayam. So the workmen built the temple of the Lord.
And the Priests stood arayed in their vestiments with musicall instruments, and trumpets, and the Leuites the sons of Asaph had Cymbals,
Singing songs of thanksgiuing, and praising the Lord according as Dauid the king of Yahsharala had ordained.
And they sung with loud voices songs to the praise of the Lord: because his mercy and glory is for ever in all Yahsharala.
And all the people sounded trumpets, and shouted with a loud voyce, singing songs of thankesgiuing to the Lord for the rearing up of the house of the Lord.
Also of the Priests and Leuites, and of the chiefe of their families the ancients who had seene the former house, came to the building of this with weeping and great crying.
But many with trumpets and ioy shouted with loud voyce.
Insomuch that the trumpets might not be heard for the weeping of the people: yet the multitude sounded marueilously, so that it was heard a farre off.
Therefore when the enemies of the Tribe of Iuda and Beniamin heard it, they came to know what that noise of trumpets should meane.
And they perceiued, that they that were of the captiuity did build the temple to the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala.
So they went to Zorobabel and Jesus, and to the chiefe of the families, and said to them, We will build together with you.
For we likewise, as you, do obey your Lord, and do sacrifice to him from the days of Asbazareth the king of the Assyrians who brought us hither
Then Zorobabel and Jesus, and the chiefe of the families of Yahsharala said to them, It is not for us and you to build together an house to the Lord our Alahayam.
We our selues alone will build to the Lord of Yahsharala, according as Cyrus the King of the Persians has commanded us.
But the heathen of the land lying heauy on the inhabitants of Iudea, and holding them straite, hindred their building:

And by their secret plots, and popular perswasions, and commotions, they hindred the finishing of the building, all the time that king Cyrus lived, so they were hindered from building for the space of two yeeres, until the reigne of Darius.

Now in the second yeere of the reigne of Darius, Aggeus, and Zacharias the son of Addo, the prophets prophesied to the Jews, in Iurie and Jerusalem in the Name of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala which was on them.
Then stood up Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Iosedec, and beganne to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, the prophets of the Lord being with them,and helping them.
At the same time came to them Sisinnes the gouernor of Syria, and Phenice, with Sathrabuzanes, and his companions, and said to them,
By whose appointment do you build this house, and this roofe, and performe all the other things? and who are the workemen that performe these things?
Neuerthelesse the Elders of the Jews obtained favor: because the Lord had visited the captiuitie.
And they were not hindred from building vntil such time as signification was given to Darius concerning them, and an answere received.
The copie of the letters which Sisinnes gouernour of Syria, and Phenice, and Sathrabuzanes with their companions rulers in Syria and Phenice, wrote and sent to Darius, To king Darius, greeting.

Let all things be knowen to our lord the King, that being come into the country of Iudea, and entred into the city of Jerusalem, we found in the city of Jerusalem the ancients of the Jews that were of the captiuitie;
Building an house to the Lord, great, and newe, of hewen and costly stones, and the timber already laid on the walles.
And those workes are done with great speede, and the worke goes on prosperously in their handes, and with all glory and diligence is it made.
Then asked we these Elders, saying, By whose commaundement builde you this house, and lay the foundations of these workes?
Therefore to the intent that we might give knowledge to you by writing, we demanded of them who were the chiefe doers, and we required of them the names in writing of their principall men.
So they gave us this answere: We are the servants of the Lord which made heaven and earth.
And as for this house, it was builded many yeeres agoe, by a king of Yahsharala great and strong, and was finished.
But when our fathers prouoked Alahayam to wrath, and sinned against the Lord of Yahsharala which is in heaven, he gave them over into the power of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon of the Chaldees:
Who pulled down the house and burnt it, and caried away the people captiues to Babylon.
But in the first yeere that King Cyrus reigned over the country of Babylon, Cyrus the king wrote to build up this house.

And the holy vessels of gold and of siluer, that Nabuchodonosor had caried away out of the house at Jerusalem, and had set them in his own temple, those Cyrus the king brought forth again out of the temple at Babylon, and they were deliuered to Zorobabel and to Sanabassarus the ruler,
With commaundement that he should carrie away the same vessels, and put them in the Temple at Jerusalem, and that the Temple of þ Lord should be built in his place.
Then the same Sanabassarus being come hither, laid the foundations of the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, and from that time to this, being still a building, it is not yet fully ended.
Now therefore if it seeme good to the king, let search be made among the records of King Cyrus,
And if it be found, that the building of the house of the Lord at Jerusalem has been done with the consent of King Cyrus, and if our lord the king be so minded, let him signifie to us of it.
Then commanded king Darius to seeke among the records at Babylon: and so at Ecbatana the palace which is in the country of Media, there was found a roule in which these things were recorded.
In the first yeere of the reigne of Cyrus, king Cyrus commaunded that the house of the Lord at Jerusalem should be built again where they do sacrifice with continuall fire.

Whose height shall be sixtie cubits, and the breadth sixtie cubits, with three rowes of hewen stones, and one row of new wood of that country, and the expenses of it to be given out of the house of king Cyrus.

And that the holy vessels of the house of the Lord, both of gold and siluer that Nabuchodonosor tooke out of the house at Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, should be restored to the house at Jerusalem, and be set in the place where they were before.

And also he commanded that Sisinnes the gouernour of Syria and Phenice, and Sathrabuzanes, and their companions, and those which were appointed rulers in Syria, and Phenice should be carefull not to meddle with the place, but suffer Zorobabel the servant of the Lord, and gouernour of Iudea, and the Elders of the Jews, to build the house of the Lord in that place.
I have commanded also to have it built up whole again, and that they looke diligently to helpe those that be of the captiuitie of the Jews, till the house of the Lord be finished.
And out of the tribute of Coelosyria, and Phenice, a portion carefully to be given these men, for the sacrifices of the Lord that is, to Zorobabel the gouernour, for bullocks, and rammes, and lambes;
And also corne, salt, wine and oile, and that continually every yeere without further question, according as the Priests that be in Jerusalem shall signifie, to be daily spent:
That offrings may be made to the most high Alahayam, for the king and for his children, and that they may pray for their liues.

And he commanded, that whoever should transgresse, yea, or make light of any thing afore spoken or written, out of his own house should a tree be taken, and he thereon be hanged, and all his goods seized for the king.
The Lord therfore whose Name is there called on, vtterly destroy every king and nation, that stretcheth out his hand to hinder or endammage that house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
I Darius the king have ordeined, that according to these things it be done with diligence.
Then Sisinnes the gouernour of Coelosyria, and Phenice, and Sathrabuzanes, with their companions, following the commandements of king Darius,
Did very carefully ouersee the holy workes, assisting the ancients of the Jews, & gouernours of the Temple.
And so the holy workes prospered, when Aggeus, and Zacharias the Prophets prophecied.
And they finished these things, by the commandement of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala, and with the consent of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.
And thus was the holy house finished, in the three and twentieth day of the moneth Adar, in the sixt yeere of Darius king of the Persians.
And the children of Yahsharala: the Priests, and the Leuites, and other that were of the captiuitie, that were added to them, did according to the things written in the book of Moses.
And to the dedication of the Temple of the Lord, they offered an hundred bullockes, two hundred rammes, four hundred lambes;
And twelue goats for the sin of all Yahsharala, according to the number of the chiefe of the tribes of Yahsharala.

The Priests also and the Leuites, stood arayed in their vestments according to their kinreds, in the seruices of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala, according to the book of Moses: and the porters at every gate.
And the children of Yahsharala that were of the captiuitie, held the Passeouer the fourteenth day of the first moueth, after that the Priests and the Leuites were sanctified.
They that were of the captiuitie were not all sanctified together: but the Leuites were all sanctified together,
And so they offered the Passeouer for all them of the captiuitie, and for their brothers the Priestes, and for themselues.
And the children of Yahsharala that came out of the captiuitie, did eate, even all they that had separated themselues from the abominations of the people of the land, and sought the Lord.
And they kept the feast of vnleauened bread seven days, making mercy before the Lord,
For that he had turned the counsell of the King of Assyria towards them to strengthen their hands in the workes of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala.
And after these things, when Artaxerxes the king of the Persians reigned, came Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Ezerias, the son of Helchiah, the son of Salum,

The son of Sadduc, the son of Achitob, the son of Amarias, the son of Ozias, the son of Memeroth, the son of Zaraias, the son of Sauias, the son of Boccas, the son of Abisum, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleasar, the son of Aaron the chiefe Priest.
This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a Scribe being very ready in the Law of Moyses, that was given by the Alahayam of Yahsharala,
And the king did him honour: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests.
There went up with him also certain of the children of Yahsharala, of the Priests, of the Leuites, of the holy Singers, Porters, and Ministers of the Temple, to Jerusalem,

In the seventh yere of the reigne of king Artaxerxes, in the fifth moneth, (this was the kings seventh yeere) for they went from Babylon in the first day of the first moneth, and came to Jerusalem, according to the prosperous iourney which the Lord gave them.
For Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the Law and Commaundements of the Lord, but taught all Yahsharala the Ordinances and Iudgements.
Now the copy of the Commission which was written from Artaxerxes the King, and came to Esdras the priest and reader of the Law of the Lord, is this that followeth.
King Artaxerxes to Esdras the Priest and reader of the Law of the Lord, sendeth greeting.

Hauing determined to deale graciously, I have given order, that such of the nation of the Jews, and of the Priests and Leuites being within our Realme, as are willing and desirous, should goe with you to Jerusalem.
As many therefore as have a mind thereunto, let them depart with you, as it has seemed good both to me, & my seven friends the counsellors,
That they may looke to the affaires of Iudea and Jerusalem, agreeably to that which is in the Law of the Lord.
And cary the gifts to the Lord of Yahsharala to Jerusalem, which I and my friends have vowed, and all the golde and siluer that in the country of Babylon can be found, to the Lord in Jerusalem,

With that also which is given of the people, for the Temple of the Lord their Alahayam at Jerusalem: and that siluer and golde may be collected for bullocks, rammes and lambes, and things thereunto appertaining,
To the end that they may offer sacrifices to the Lord, on the Altar of the Lord their Alahayam, which is in Jerusalem.
And whatsoeuer you and your brothers will do with the siluer and golde, that do according to the will of your Alahayam.
And the holy vessels of the Lord which are given you, for the use of the Temple of your Alahayam which is in Jerusalem, you will set before your Alahayam in Jerusalem.
And whatsoeuer thing else you will remember for the use of the Temple of your Alahayam, you will give it out of the kings treasury.

And I, king Artaxerxes, have also commaunded the keepers of the treasures in Syria and Phenice, that whatsoeuer Esdras the priest, and the reader of the law of the most high Alahayam shall send for, they should give it him with speed,
To the summe of an hundred talents of siluer: likewise also of wheat even to an hundred cores, and an hundred pieces of wine, and other things in abundance.
Let all things be performed after the law of Alahayam diligently to the most high Alahayam, that wrath come not on the kingdome of the King and his sons.

I command you also that you require no taxe, nor any other imposition of any of the Priests or Leuites, or holy singers, or porters, or ministers of the temple, or of any that have doings in this temple, and that no man have authority to impose any thing on them.

And you, Esdras, according to the wisedome of Alahayam, ordaine iudges, and iustices, that they may judge in all Syria and Phenice, all those that know the law of your Alahayam, and those that know it not you will teach.
And whoever shall transgresse the law of your Alahayam, and of the king, shall be punished diligently, whether it be by death or other punishment, by penalty of money, or by imprisonment.
¶ Then said Esdras the Scribe, Blessed be the only Lord Alahayam of my fathers, who has put these things into the heart of the king, to glorifie his house that is in Jerusalem;
And has honoured mee in the sight of the king and his counsellers, and all his friends and Nobles.
Therefore was I encouraged, by the helpe of the Lord my Alahayam, and gathered together men of Yahsharala to goe up with me:
And these are the chiefe according to their families and seuerall dignities, that went up with me from Babylon in the reigne of king Artaxerxes.
Of the sons of Phinees, Gerson: of the sons of Ithamar, Gamael: of the sons of Dauid; Lettus the son of Sechenias:
Of the sons of Pharez, Zacharias, and with him were counted, an hundred and fifty men:
Of the sons of Pahath, Moab; Eliaonias, the son of Zaraias, and with him two hundred men:
Of the sons of Zathoe, Sechenias, the son of Iezelus, and with him three hundred men, Of the sons of Adin, Obeth the son of Ionathan, and with him two hundred and fifty men.
Of the sons of Elam, Josias son of Gotholias, and with him seuenty men:
Of the sons of Saphatias, Zaraias son of Michael, and with him threescore and ten men:
Of the sons of Ioab, Abadias son of Iezelus, and with him two hundred and twelue men:
Of the sons of Banid, Assalimoth son of Iosaphias, and with him an hundred and threescore men:
Of the sons of Babi, Zacharias son of Bebai, and with him twenty and eight men:
Of the sons of Astath, Iohannessonne of Acatan, and with him an hundred and ten men:
Of the sons of Adonicam the last, and these are the names of them, Eliphalet, Ieuel, and Samaias and with them seuenty men:
Of the sons of Bago, Uthi, the son of Istalcurus, and with him seuenty men:
And these I gathered together to the riuer, called Theras, where we pitched our tents three days, and then I suruayed them.
But when I had found there, none of the priests and Leuites,
Then sent I to Eleazar and Iduel, and Masman,
And Alnathan, and Mamaias, and Ioribas, and Nathan, Eunatan, Zacharias, and Mosollamon principal men and learned.
And I bad them that they should goe to Saddeus the captaine, who was in the place of the treasury:
And commanded them that they should speak to Daddeus, and to his brothers, and to the treasurers in that place, to send us such men as might execute the Priests office in the house of the Lord.
And by the mighty hand of our Lord they brought to us skilful men of the sons of Moli, the son of Leui, the son of Yahsharala, Asebebia and his sons and his brothers, who were eighteene.
And Asebia, and Annuus, and Osaias his brother of the sons of Channuneus, and their sons were twenty men.

And of the servants of the Temple whom Dauid had ordeined, and the principall men, for the seruice of the Leuites (to wit) the servants of the Temple, two hundred and twenty, the catalogue of whose names were showed.
And there I vowed a fast to the yong men before our Lord, to desire of him a prosperous iourney, both for us, and them that were with us: for our children and for the cattell:
For I was ashamed to aske the king footmen, & horsemen, and conduct for safegard against our aduersaries:
For we had said to the king, that the power of the Lord our Alahayam, should be with them that seeke him, to support them in all ways.
And again we besought our Lord, as touching these things, & found him fauourable to us.
Then I separated twelue of the chiefe of the priests, Esebrias, & Assanias, and ten men of their brothers with them.
And I weighed them the golde, and the siluer, and the holy vessels of the house of our Lord, which the king and his counsell, and the princes, and all Yahsharala had given.
And when I had weighed it, I deliuered to them six hundred and fifty talents of siluer, and siluer vessels of an hundred talents, and an hundred talents of gold,
And twenty golden vessels, and twelue vessels of brasse, even of fine brasse, glittering like gold.
And I said to them, Both you are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the golde, and the siluer isa vowe to the Lord, the Lord of our fathers.

Watch you, and keepe them till you deliuer them to the chiefe of the priestes and Leuites, and to the principall men of the families of Yahsharala in Jerusalem into the chambers of the house of our Alahayam.
So the priests and the Leuites who had received the siluer & the golde, and the vessels, brought them to Jerusalem into the Temple of the Lord.

And from the riuer Theras we departed the twelft day of the first moneth, and came to Jerusalem by the mightie hand of our Lord, which was with us: and from the beginning of our iourney, the Lord deliuered us from every enemy, and so we came to Jerusalem.
And when we had been there three days, the golde and siluer that was weighed, was deliuered in the house of our Lord on the fourth day to Marmoth the priest, the son of Iri.
And with him was Eleazar the son of Phinees, and with them were Iosabad the son of Iesu, and Moeth the son of Sabban, Leuites: all was deliuered them by number and weight.
And all the weight of them was written up the same houre.
Moreouer they that were come out of the captiuitie offered sacrifice to the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala, even twelue bullocks for all Yahsharala, fourescore and sixteene rammes,
Threescore and twelue lambes, goates for a peace offering, twelue, all of them a sacrifice to the Lord.
And they deliuered the kings commandements to the kings stewards, and to the gouernours of Coelosyria, and Phenice, and they honoured the people, and the Temple of Alahayam.
Now when these things were done, the rulers came to me, and said:

The nation of Yahsharala, the princes, the priests, and Leuites have not put away from them the strange people of the land: nor the pollutions of the Gentiles, to wit, of the Chanaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Iebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.

For both they, and their sons, have maried with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land, and from the beginning of this matter, the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquitie.
And assoone as I had heard these things, I rent my clothes, and the holy garment, and pulled off the haire from off my head, and beard, and sate me down sad, and very heauy.

So all they that were then mooued at the word of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala, assembled to me, whilest I mourned for the iniquitie: but I sate still full of heauinesse, until the euening sacrifice.
Then rising up from the fast with my clothes and the holy garment rent, and bowing my knees, and stretching foorth my hands to the Lord:
I said, O Lord, I am confounded, and ashamed before your face;
For our sins are multiplied above our heads, and our ignorances have reached up to heaven.
For ever since the time of our fathers we have been and are in great sin, even to this day:

And for our sins and our fathers, we with our brothers, and our kings, and our priests, were given up to the Kings of the earth, to the sword, and to captiuitie, and for a pray with shame, to this day.
And now in some measure has mercy been showed to us, from you, O Lord, that there should be left us a roote, and a name, in the place of your Sanctuary.
And to discouer to us a light in the house of the Lord our Alahayam, and to give us foode in the time of our seruitude.
Yea, when we were in bondage, we were not forsaken of our Lord; but he made us gracious before the Kings of Persia, so that they gave us food;
Yea, and honoured the Temple of our Lord, and raised up the desolate Sion, that they have given us a sure abiding in Iurie, and Jerusalem.
And now, O Lord, what shall we say hauing these things? for we have transgressed your Commaundements, which you gauest by the hand of your servants the Prophets, saying,
That the land which you enter into to possesse as an heritage, is a land polluted with the pollutions of the strangers of the land, and they have filled it with their vncleannesse.
Therefore now shall you not ioyne your daughters to their sons, neither shall you take their daughters to your sons.
Moreouer you shall never seeke to have peace with them, that you may be strong, and eate the good things of the land, and that you may leaue the inheritance of the land to your children for euermore.
And all that is befallen, is done to us for our wicked workes, and great sins: for you, O Lord, did make our sins light:
And did give to us such a roote: but we have turned backe again to transgresse your Law, and to mingle our selues with the vncleannesse of the nations of the land.
Might not you be angry with us to destroy us, till you hadst left us neither root, seed, nor name?
O Lord of Yahsharala, you are true: for we are left a root this day.
Behold, now are we before you in our iniquities, for we cannot stand any longer by reason of these things before you.

And as Esdras in his praier made his confession, weeping, and lying flat on the ground before the Temple, there gathered to him from Jerusalem, a very great multitude of men, and women, & children: for there was great weeping among the multitude.

Then Iechonias the son of Ieelus, one of the sons of Yahsharala called out and saide, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord Alahayam, we have maried strange women of the nations of the land, & now is all Yahsharala aloft.
Let us make an oath to the Lord, that we will put away all our wiues, which we have taken of the heathen, with their children,
Like as you have decreed, and as many as do obey the Law of the Lord.
Arise, and put in execution: for to you does this matter appertaine, and we will be with you: do valiantly.
So Esdras arose, and tooke an oath of the chiefe of the Priestes, and Leuites of all Yahsharala, to do after these things, and so they sware.
Then Esdras rising from the court of the Temple, went to the chamber of Ioanan the son of Eliasib,
And remained there, and did eate no meate nor drinke water, mourning for the great iniquities of the multitude.
And there was a proclamation in all Iury and Jerusalem, to all them that were of the captiuitie, that they should be gathered together at Jerusalem:

And that whoever met not there within two or three days according as the Elders that bare rule, appointed, their cattell should be seized to the use of the Temple, and himself cast out from them that were of the captiuitie.
And in three days were all they of the tribe of Iuda and Beniamin gathered together at Jerusalem the twentieth day of the ninth moneth.
And all the multitude sate trembling in the broad court of the Temple, because of the present foule weather.
So Esdras arose up, and said to them, You have transgressed the law in marrying strange wiues, thereby to increase the sins of Yahsharala.
And now by confessing give glory to the Lord Alahayam of our fathers,
And do his will, and separate your selues from the heathen of the land, and from the strange women.
Then cryed the whole multitude, and sayd with a loude voice; Like as you have spoken, so will we do.
But forasmuch as the people are many, and it is foule weather, so that we cannot stand without, and this is not a worke of a day or two, seeing our sin in these things is spread farre:
Therefore let the rulers of the multitude stay, and let all them of our habitations that have strange wiues, come at the time appointed,
And with them the Rulers and Iudges of every place, till we turne away the wrath of the Lord from us, for this matter.
Then Ionathan the son of Azael, and Ezechias the son of Theocanus, accordingly tooke this matter on them: and Mosollam, and Leuis, and Sabbatheus helped them.
And they that were of the captiutie, did according to all these things.
And Esdras the Priest chose to him the principal men of their families, all by name: and in the first day of the tenth moneth, they sate together to examine the matter.
So their cause that helde strange wiues, was brought to an ende in the first day of the first moneth.
And of the Priests that were come together, and had strange wiues, there were found:
Of the sons of Jesus the son of Iosedec, and his brothers, Matthelas, and Eleazar, and Ioribus, and Ioadanus.
And they gave their hands to put away their wiues, & to offer rammes, to make reconcilement for their errors.
And of the sons of Emmer, Ananias, and Zabdeus, and Eanes, and Sameius, and Hierel, and Azarias.
And of the sons of Phaisur, Ellionas, Massias, Ismael, and Nathanael, and Oridelus, and Talsas.
And of the Leuites: Iosabad, and Semis, and Colius who was called Calitas, and Patheus, and Judas, and Ionas.
Of the holy Singers: Eleazurus, Bacchurus.
Of the Porters: Sallumus, and Tolbanes.
Of them of Yahsharala, of the sons of Phoros, Hiermas, and Eddias, and Melchias, and Maelus, and Eleazar, and Asibias, and Baanias.
Of the sons of Ela, Matthanias, Zacharias, and Hierielus, and Hieremoth, and Aedias.
And of the sons of Zamoth, Eliadas, Elisimus, Othonias, Iarimoth, and Sabatus, and Sardeus.
Of the sons of Bebai, Iohannes, and Ananias, and Iosabad, and Amatheis.
Of the sons of Many, Olamus, Mamuchus, Iedeus, Iasubus, Iasael, and Hieremoth.
And of the sons of Addi, Naathus, and Moosias, Lacunus, and Naidus, and Mathanias, and Sesthel, Balunus, and Manasseas.
And of the sons of Annas, Elionas, and Aseas, and Milchias, and Sabbeus, and Simon Chosameus.
And of the sons of Asom, Altaneus, and Matthias, and Bannaia, Eliphalat, and Manasses, and Semei.

And of the sons of Maani, Ieremias, Momdis, Omaerus, Iuel, Mabdai, and Pelias, and Anos, Carabasion, and Enasibus, & Mamnitanaimus, Eliasis, Bannus, Eliali, Samis, Selenias, Nathanias: And of the sons of Ozora, Sesis, Esril, Azailus, Samatus, Zambis, Iosiphus,
And of the sons of Ethma, Mazitias, Zabadaias, Edes, Iuel, Banaias.
All these had taken strange wiues, and they put them away with their children.
And the priests, and Leuites, and they that were of Yahsharala dwelt in Jerusalem, and in the country, in the first day of þ seventh month: so the children of Yahsharala were in their habitations.
And the whole multitude came together with one accord, into the broad place of the holy porch toward the East.
And they spake to Esdras the priest and reader, that he would bring the law of Moses, that was given of the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala.
So Esdras the chiefe priest, brought the law to the whole multitude from man to woman, and to all the priests, to heare the law in the first day of the seventh moneth.
And he read in the broad court before the holy porch from morning to midday, before both men and women; and all the multitude gave heed to the law.
And Esdras the priest, and reader of the law stood up, on a pulpit of wood which was made for that purpose.
And there stood up by him Matathias, Sammus, Ananias, Azarias, Urias, Ezecias, Balasamus, on the right hand.
And on his left hand stood Phaldaius, Misael, Melchias, Lothasubus and Nabarias.
Then tooke Esdras the book of the law before the multitude: for he sate honourably in the first place in the sight of them all.
And when he opened the law, they stood all streight up. So Esdras blessed the Lord Alahayam most high, the Alahayam of hostes Almighty.
And all the people answered Amen, and lifting up their hands they fell to the ground, & worshipped the Lord.

Also Jesus, Anus, Sarabias, Adinus, Iacubus, Sabateus, Auteas, Maianeas, and Calitas, Azarias, and Ioazabdus, and Ananias, Biatas, the Leuites taught the law of the Lord, making them withall to understand it.
Then spake Attharates to Esdras the chiefe priest, and reader, and to the Leuites that taught the multitude, even to all, saying,
This day is holy to þ Lord; for they all wept when they heard the law.
Goe then and eate the fat, and drinke the sweet, and send part to them that have nothing.
For this day is holy to the Lord, and be not sorrowfull; for the Lord will bring you to honour.
So the Leuites published all things to the people, saying: This day is holy to the Lord, be not sorrowfull.
Then went they their way, every one to eate and drinke, & make mery, and to give part to them that had nothing, and to make great cheere,
Because they vnderstood the words in which they were instructed, and for þ which they had bin assembled.
